text:
maria.gomez: Heads-up — running a quick cross-run of the same v1.2.3 model on hosted vs our VPC cluster and seeing ~30% lower throughput on the private nodes (hosted: ~1.2k tok/s, vpc: ~850 tok/s). Can folks help triage?

jonathan.lee: ack. do you have the exact command/flags and model config used? batch/seq len?

maria.gomez: same workload: batch_size=4, max_len=1024, kv cache warm, quant=4bit-fp8-sim, streaming disabled. Request payloads identical. Running the standard bench harness: `./bench --model v1.2.3 --batch 4 --len 1024 --iters 200`

samir.khan: quick checks: kernel version, cpu governor, and NIC offload state often cause these gaps. Also whether irqbalance is enabled and if cpuset or cgroup cpusets differ.

oliver: +1. did you run with vs without hugepages? also check numa placement. on our onprem images we've seen fallback to single-node NUMA for some docker runtimes.

maria.gomez: attaching nodes details and perf logs here: https://redwood-internal/storage/runs/1861234567/ (flamegraph + raw logs). kernel on vpc nodes: 5.15.0-58, hosted: 5.19.0-3. Docker runtime is containerd on both. hugepages: enabled on hosted, not on vpc.

jonathan.lee: that alone could explain a lot. can you paste outputs of these commands?

```
# on vpc node
uname -a
lscpu
cat /sys/kernel/mm/hugepages/hugepages-2048kB/nr_hugepages
etstat -i
ethtool -k eth0
```

samir.khan: Also run `sudo perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-misses -a -- ./bench ...` for a short run to check if we have more stalls/cache misses.

infra-bot: CI bench job queued: bench/v1.2.3/quick/1861234567. Results will be posted when finished. :gear:

oliver: if hugepages differ, try enabling on a single node and re-run. On past infra we've seen 15-35% wins for large models. Also confirm transparent hugepages (THP) status and vm.swappiness.

maria.gomez: pasted outputs (excerpt):
```
# lscpu
Architecture: x86_64
CPU(s): 64
NUMA nodes: 2
Model name: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Gold 6338

# nr_hugepages = 0
# ethtool -k eth0
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
udp-fragmentation-offload: off
```

jonathan.lee: nr_hugepages=0 is a red flag. Also udp-fragmentation-offload off is fine. Check NIC interrupt distribution: `cat /proc/interrupts | grep eth0` and `ls -l /sys/class/net/eth0/device/` for irq_affinity.

samir.khan: can you also confirm the CUDA/cuDNN versions? mismatch there can lower kernel perf. `nvidia-smi` + `python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.backends.cudnn.version())'`

maria.gomez: CUDA is 11.8 on both, torch reports 2.1.0 on hosted, 2.1.0 on vpc as well. cuDNN 8.1 everywhere.

oliver: ok. next hypothesis: kernel scheduler and cpufreq. What's `cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor` showing? If set to "powersave" that can bite bursty inference.

maria.gomez: gov is "performance" on hosted, "ondemand" on vpc.

jonathan.lee: switch ondemand -> performance for a test and re-run. Also try pinning server process to a single NUMA socket to see if remote memory accesses are causing latency. Example: `taskset -c 0-31 ./bench ...` vs `32-63`

samir.khan: another quick check: are we running the same kernel perf optimizations? e.g., `sysctl net.core.rmem_max` and `net.ipv4.tcp_rmem` can affect large payloads. Run `sysctl -a | egrep "rmem|wmem|tcp_rmem|tcp_wmem"`

maria.gomez: made changes on a staging node: enabled hugepages (2G not available, did 2MB), set governor to performance, pinned process to socket 0. Re-ran a 50-iter quick bench -> throughput jumped from 850 -> 1.05k tok/s. Not fully parity but significantly closer.

oliver: good signal. next steps: propose a small runbook to align kernel params and numa configs for private images. We should also add a preflight check to the bench harness to log these and warn if mismatch.

jonathan.lee: agree. I can draft a PR to the bench harness that: (1) captures sysctl, hugepages, governor, irq distribution; (2) optionally toggles hugepages and reports delta; and (3) uploads flamegraphs to S3.

samir.khan: I'll follow up with a patch to our image builder to enable hugepages and set governor by default for our inference AMIs. Need a quick owner review if there are security implications.

maria.gomez: thanks all. Can we reconvene async here when PRs are up? I'll re-run a full 200-iter with the aligned config and post results. :white_check_mark:
